data.title: China's Industrial Profit Surged Despite Headwinds
data.description:
China's industrial profit surged in October despite mounting domestic headwinds, as robust global demand for its tech products continued to turbocharge exports.

Profits at China's major industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier in October, accelerating from the prior month's 14.4% growth, according to official data released Friday. During the first 10 months of the year, China's industrial profit jumped 16.0%.

Profit growth was powered by the electronics sector, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Rising demand for artificial-intelligence computing power drove sustained profit gains across related industries, including memory chips and peripheral manufacturing, said Yu Weining, a senior official at the bureau.

During the January-to-October period, profits in the electronics sector doubled from a year earlier, contributing roughly 10 percentage points to overall profit growth among major industrial firms and serving as a key driver of their rapid expansion, said Yu.

Rapid growth in the new-energy and AI sectors also fueled strong demand and higher prices for base metals such as copper and aluminum from January to October, pushing profits up 60.2% from a year earlier in nonferrous metal mining and 71.7% across the broader nonferrous metals industry.

Friday's upbeat data contrasted with earlier data showing the world's second-largest economy lost momentum across multiple fronts in October, underscoring its uneven growth. Surging exports have obscured sluggish consumer demand, declining investment and a protracted property downturn.

Economists at ANZ said China's robust exports have failed to pass through to domestic demand. "Weak domestic demand has exacerbated both domestic and global imbalances, while persistent disinflation has kept onshore yields structurally low." they told clients in a note Friday.

data.title: Asian Markets Mostly Higher as Sentiment Stabilizes
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Asian markets were mostly higher Friday, tracking gains in U.S. stock futures as sentiment around artificial intelligence stabilized.

"U.S. markets were closed for Thanksgiving, leaving global markets to trade largely off the late recovery on Wall Street in Wednesday's session," said Westpac's Neha Sharma in an email.

Asian markets have also taken cues from stronger U.S. stock futures. E-mini Nasdaq futures were up 1.3%, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.0% and 0.7%, respectively.

South Korea's Kospi rose 1.65% and Japan's Nikkei Stock Average rose 0.7%. China's Shanghai Composite Index added 0.2% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.2% higher. However, Taiwan's Taiex bucked the trend to drop 0.3%.

The gains came even as Nvidia ordered its manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, after the U.S. escalated its push to keep the company's AI chips out of China's hands, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Oil prices were mixed after rallying overnight. Iran has stepped up its strikes targeting some of its Gulf neighbors and ships trying to get oil and natural gas out through the Strait of Hormuz. Most recently, an Iranian drone attack on Kuwait killed two Italians performing maintenance on antidrone equipment, authorities said.

Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthi militant group attacked Saudi Arabia's Jazan oil refinery on Thursday and killed one worker, the kingdom's Ministry of Energy said in a statement.

The attacks offset hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, ANZ Research analysts said in a note.

However, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week in the seven days through Nov. 20, while gasoline and distillate stockpiles also increased, according to the latest data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude-oil futures rose 2.1% to $85.41 a barrel, while front-month Brent was down 0.4% at $96.20 a barrel, according to ICE data.

data.title: SkyDrive Partners With HeliKorea and Verty to Build eVTOL Operations, Maintenance and Training Ecosystem in South Korea
data.description:
SkyDrive Partners With HeliKorea and Verty to Build eVTOL Operations, Maintenance and Training Ecosystem in South Korea

Partnership with one of Korea’s leading helicopter operators advances SkyDrive’s commercial eVTOL plans in the country

SkyDrive Inc. (“SkyDrive”), a leading compact eVTOL aircraft (*1) developer based in Japan, announced that it has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with HeliKorea Co., Ltd. (“HeliKorea”), a Daejeon-based company and one of South Korea’s leading private helicopter operators, and Verty Co., Ltd. (“Verty”), a Seoul-based eVTOL operator leading initial flight demonstrations and providing an integrated operating system linking flight operations, traffic management and vertiport operations. Under the agreement, the three companies will work together to build an eVTOL ecosystem in South Korea and lay the groundwork for commercial service — setting up frameworks to introduce and operate eVTOL aircraft, conduct maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) and train pilots, mechanics and other specialists. Building on this partnership, SkyDrive aims to launch commercial eVTOL services in South Korea.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261126491652/en/

From left: Youngsu Yi, overseas business development South Korea representative at SkyDrive; Gang-Im Lee, executive vice president of HeliKorea; and Dong-Woo Kim, CEO of Verty.

Building an eVTOL Ecosystem in South Korea

Guided by its mission “to take the lead in the once-in-a-century mobility revolution,” SkyDrive is developing and manufacturing compact eVTOL aircraft to make urban air travel part of everyday life. In South Korea, where the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) has set out a roadmap to begin commercial eVTOL operations in 2028, SkyDrive views the country as one of its priority markets for global expansion.

SkyDrive has been building its partner network in South Korea step by step. In Sept. 2026, it signed an MOU with Verty (*2) to begin exploring the introduction and commercial operation of SKYDRIVE (SD-05 model) in the South Korean market. In Nov. 2026, the two companies signed a three-party MOU (*3) with Goyang Special City, which is developing vertiports to serve as the Seoul metropolitan area’s demonstration hub for the national Korean Urban Air Mobility program. Through this public-private partnership, the city and the companies are working together to prepare the environment for demonstration and trial flights as well as commercial operations in Goyang.

Aircraft, vertiports and operating systems are not enough on their own for safe, ongoing commercial eVTOL service. Operators also need teams to run daily flights, MRO capabilities to keep aircraft airworthy and training programs that develop pilots, maintenance technicians and other specialists.

With 30 years of experience since its founding in 1996, HeliKorea has delivered a wide range of aviation services as one of South Korea’s leading private helicopter operators. Its operations span air ambulance missions with the Ministry of Health and Welfare, wildfire suppression for local governments, cargo transport, pilot training as an approved training organization (ATO) and helicopter MRO services for public agencies. Its long-standing operational, maintenance and training expertise will support initial eVTOL flight demonstrations and help expand flight services once commercial operations begin.

Against this backdrop, SkyDrive, Verty and HeliKorea agreed to enter into this operational agreement, combining SkyDrive’s aircraft manufacturing, Verty’s initial flight demonstrations and integrated operating system, and HeliKorea’s helicopter operations, maintenance and training expertise. Through this collaboration, SkyDrive is advancing partnerships across key pillars of South Korea’s eVTOL ecosystem: aircraft, vertiports, operating systems, flight operations, MRO and training. SkyDrive will continue adding partners as it works toward commercial service.

Key Areas of Cooperation

HeliKorea, Verty and SkyDrive will cooperate in the following areas to build South Korea’s eVTOL ecosystem and establish the foundation for commercialization:

  • Supporting the growth and revitalization of South Korea’s eVTOL industry
  • Advancing demonstration flights, trial operations and commercialization of eVTOL services in South Korea
  • Building frameworks for eVTOL introduction, flight operations, MRO and training
  • Identifying and examining joint initiatives that draw on each company’s specialized strengths
  • Pursuing other cooperation in aviation and eVTOL fields as agreed by the three companies

The three companies will also divide roles and cooperate by commercialization phase as follows:

  • Initial demonstration phase: Verty will conduct initial flight demonstrations toward commercialization and provide its integrated operating system. HeliKorea will draw on its hands-on helicopter operations and maintenance experience to support and validate Verty’s flight demonstrations. SkyDrive will supply aircraft and provide technical support as the three companies work together to build an eVTOL ecosystem covering flight operations, MRO and training.
  • Commercialization and market expansion phase: Once the ecosystem is established, Verty and HeliKorea plan to work together to expand flight services and drive growth in South Korea’s eVTOL market.

Executive Comments

Kyongjo Min, CEO of HeliKorea Co., Ltd.
“Since our founding in 1996, HeliKorea has been keeping Korea’s skies working for people through emergency medical services, wildfire firefighting and passenger and cargo transport. We’ve spent 30 years flying and maintaining vertical takeoff aircraft, and I’m confident that experience carries straight over to safe eVTOL operations, maintenance and workforce training. With this agreement, we’ll connect SkyDrive’s aircraft technology and Verty’s operational and infrastructure capabilities with HeliKorea’s hands-on experience to build the foundation for commercial eVTOL service here in Korea step by step.”

Dong-Woo Kim, CEO of Verty Co., Ltd.
“Following our agreements with SkyDrive and Goyang Special City, it means a lot to now be working with HeliKorea, a company that has been flying and maintaining helicopters since 1996. Commercial eVTOL service can’t start with aircraft alone — it takes daily operations, maintenance and the pilots and technicians behind all of it. As Korea’s eVTOL operator, Verty takes responsibility for operations and maintenance while bringing traffic management and vertiport operations together under one system. We’ll work closely with HeliKorea across operations, maintenance and training so that their years of helicopter experience feed directly into how we run eVTOL flights, and together with SkyDrive’s aircraft, we’ll work to launch safe commercial eVTOL service in Korea in 2028.”

Tomohiro Fukuzawa, founder and CEO of SkyDrive Inc.
“Following our partnerships with Verty and Goyang Special City, I’m truly honored to be signing this operational agreement with HeliKorea, a company that has spent many years flying, maintaining and training on helicopters in Korea. If eVTOLs are going to become part of everyday life, aircraft and vertiports aren’t enough — you also need maintenance and training systems that keep daily flights safe. By combining SkyDrive’s aircraft, Verty’s flight demonstration capabilities and integrated operating system, and HeliKorea’s deep frontline experience, we’ll build out Korea’s eVTOL framework in stages, from initial demonstrations all the way through to growing commercial service. We’ll keep working with many more partners to build this ecosystem toward launching commercial operations in Korea.”

About HeliKorea Co., Ltd.

Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, HeliKorea is one of the country’s leading private helicopter operators. Focusing on flight operations and maintenance, the company provides a wide range of aviation services, including helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS), offshore transport, wildfire firefighting, commuter passenger air transport, cargo transport, pilot training as an approved training organization (ATO) and helicopter MRO services for public agencies.

For more information, please visit: https://www.helikorea.co.kr/

About Verty Co., Ltd.

Based in Seoul, South Korea, Verty is the only operator in the country preparing demonstrations across all three core areas of advanced air mobility (AAM): flight operations, traffic management and vertiport operations. The company is directly securing infrastructure — including aircraft, systems and specialist personnel — as it prepares to offer “AAM as a Service,” a business-to-business model that supplies flights to companies offering AAM services. Since its founding in 2018, Verty has built an in-house integrated operating system that connects the core functions needed to manage flight operations. Under this model, client companies will be able to start flying simply by submitting a flight plan without making their own infrastructure investments. Verty participates in a commercialization project led by South Korea’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) and is building the operational foundation for full-scale service in 2028.

For more information, please visit: https://www.verty.co.kr/en/

About SkyDrive Inc.

SkyDrive is a Japanese compact eVTOL company aiming "to take the lead in the once-in-a-century mobility revolution." The company began testing eVTOL prototypes in 2014 prior to official incorporation in 2018. Under its future vision for urban transportation, flying in eVTOLs will become a regular part of city life. In 2019, SkyDrive became the first company to fly a crewed eVTOL in Japan. In 2025, the company successfully showcased SKYDRIVE, the company's first commercial eVTOL product, with demonstration flights at the Osaka Expo witnessed by thousands of visitors over a one-month period. SkyDrive began production of SKYDRIVE in March 2024 at a plant owned by Suzuki Motor Corporation, SkyDrive's official production partner. SkyDrive has been working with civil aviation authorities in Japan and the U.S. to obtain certification for SKYDRIVE, with the aim of launching the aircraft into service in 2028. SkyDrive is headquartered in Toyota, Aichi Prefecture and led by CEO Tomohiro Fukuzawa, an engineer and entrepreneur.

For more information, please visit: https://skydrive.co.jp/en/

Editor’s Notes:
(*1) eVTOL is an abbreviation for electric vertical takeoff and landing. As the name suggests, eVTOL aircraft can take off and land without a runway. eVTOLs are powered by electricity and incorporate advanced, automatic, flight control technology.

 

(*2) Related press release: “SkyDrive Partners with South Korea’s Verty to Target Commercial eVTOL Operations by 2028” https://skydrive.co.jp/en/news/72971/

 

(*3) Related press release: “SkyDrive Signs MOU with Goyang Special City and Verty to Accelerate Commercial eVTOL Deployment in South Korea” https://skydrive.co.jp/en/news/73213/

 

Kaori Saito
Public Relations
SkyDrive Inc.
Email: info@skydrive.co.jp
https://skydrive.co.jp/en/contact

data.title: MISSION SUCCESS: Rocket Lab Launches 101st Electron Mission
data.description:
MAHIA, New Zealand, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today successfully completed another dedicated Electron launch for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite operator Synspective.

The ‘Night Owls Never Sleep’ mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 1:15 p.m. NZDT on 27 September 2026, delivering the 14h StriX satellite directly into a 569km low Earth orbit. This latest addition further scales Synspective’s Earth-observation constellation that gathers high-resolution images of the planet's surface regardless of weather conditions or time of day.

Today’s mission was Rocket Lab’s 22nd launch of 2026 and 101st mission overall, extending Electron’s lead as the world’s most frequently-launched small-lift orbital rocket.

Mission Highlights:

  • Unmatched Track Record: Maintaining a 100% mission success rate for Synspective, Rocket Lab has been the sole launch provider for all 14 StriX satellites to date.
  • Rapid Constellation Building: As Rocket Lab’s 22nd mission of the year, today’s launch highlights Electron’s high-cadence reliability that commercial constellation operators depend on to scale their operations on schedule.
  • Record-Breaking Partnership: Following a historic 20-launch deal signed in September - the largest commercial contract for Electron to date - Synspective is Rocket Lab’s largest launch customer with 47 total missions booked. Today’s launch leaves 33 dedicated missions on the manifest to be launched through 2031, giving Synspective long-term certainty as they build out their constellation.

data.title: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods

Jensen Huang, who on Monday returned as CEO of Nvidia. (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I was paralyzed during the market downturn, so I have a question in the event that this bounce - led by the shocking and, in my opinion, unwelcome news that Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO - does not last. No comment on that, as it happens, even though I have my opinions, like most people do.

I'm writing to you about my own strategy, not to pass judgment on other people's corporate decisions. During a market downturn, is it better for me to draw down cash from CDs for the next year or two rather than taking money from my equities and annuities at a loss? Where are the safe havens? I don't want to eat into my retirement savings.

Planning Ahead

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: America is divided into two countries - Trump's pro-billionaires and Mamdani's anti-billionaires

Being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing.

Dear Planning,

It's fair to say that many people were surprised by Jensen Huang's return on Monday - and you are not alone in having strong opinions on that.

Some of the same people who cried foul over the fall in their 401(k)s and IRAs may well be rolling their eyes over the return of Huang to the helm of Nvidia, which now appears to be the cornerstone of the AI revolution, mostly due to its multibillion-dollar microchip business and proprietary software ecosystem. Indeed, the stock gave up some of Monday's gains on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to regulatory concerns about the export of U.S. microchips to China and elsewhere. Huang was effectively fired (he officially resigned) from the company a couple of weeks ago over his reported affairs with two employees, as well as one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Commentators have questioned whether President Donald Trump overlooked the potential and alleged national-security threat by calling for Huang's return to Nvidia NVDA, thereby signaling that the company is too big to fail. Others bemoaned the decision by the company's board and wondered what the role of such boards is, if not to uphold professional, legal and personal standards. While low-wage American workers have been fired over bathroom breaks, skeptics may wonder if rules of conduct only apply to nonbillionaires.

It's OK to have joys and concerns about the billionaire class and your 401(k), even if the answers conflict with each other.

And, honestly, being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing, either. Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods. Some people panic and sell, or move into real estate, bonds, or gold, and constantly check their 401(k) while getting upset over paper losses. Yet short-term swings won't have a big impact if they aren't about to retire or haven't just retired - especially if they have cash alternatives. How many times a day or week did you check your 401(k) when the market was on the rise? I'm guessing not a lot.

I sympathize with your urge to check. According to a 2026 report by the Investment Company Institute (ICI), a global trade association representing regulated funds and their shareholders, 81% of mutual fund-owning U.S. households hold stock funds - most of them inside workplace retirement plans. Because broad stock and index funds are heavily weighted toward mega-cap AI leaders like Nvidia, a significant share of American households are naturally exposed to those stocks. "Mutual funds play a key role in their households' balance sheets," the researchers wrote.

But back to the other questions in your letter: Yes, drawing from CDs and relying on annuity income can be a smart move. That assumes you don't have required minimum distributions from a traditional retirement account and your CDs have reached the end of their term. If you paid extra for a guaranteed lifetime income rider on your annuities - locking in an income stream if markets plummet or your account balance falls to zero - that will protect you during a correction, while fixed annuities aren't tied to the market's fortunes at all. Having cash alternatives helps you avoid "sequence-of-returns risk," where poor market performance in the early years of retirement puts pressure on a portfolio you're drawing from.

Don't miss: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Is it time to sell my stocks and buy real estate?

Timing the market vs. managing risk

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, a macroeconomic research and systematic risk-management firm, predicts that markets will return to a "risk-on market regime," where investors favor higher risk assets over safe havens, within a couple of months. "Hope is not an effective risk-management process," he says. "Positioning for the market regime helps investors avoid fear of missing out (FOMO) and fear of more losses (FOML). FOMO causes investors to buy cycle tops, and FOML causes investors to sell cycle lows. These are the two worst things any investor can do to their financial well-being."

As for your curiosity about safe havens, I can understand why you would consider them after such a volatile week, especially with lingering questions about the stock market's heavy dependence on AI. The right mix depends on your risk tolerance and, as Dale suggested, your expectations about the economic outlook, especially if you want to factor in how reliant the economy is becoming on AI. There are many paths to take. Andrew Clinton, CEO of Clinton Investment Management, suggests municipal bonds as a haven during a correction.

I can understand why you would look for safe havens, especially with lingering questions about the market's heavy dependence on AI.

Municipal bonds are, for the record, more appropriate for investors in higher tax brackets with money held in taxable accounts who live in high-tax states, and for retirees prioritizing cash flow and capital preservation. "Municipal bonds offer attractive tax-adjusted carry and stable underlying asset-class credit quality for investors seeking durable cash flows amidst equity-market volatility," he says. "Current municipal bond yields remain near the most attractive levels in decades."

Clinton also has a rosier outlook on the underlying strength of the U.S. economy than, perhaps, many folks. "Credit fundamentals remain strong, with default rates representing only a fraction of corporate default rates," he says. "Municipal issuers provide essential services such as airports, utilities and toll roads, generating durable cash flows with limited exposure to corporate earnings volatility. If inflation moderates and rates decline, municipals offer the potential for both attractive income and capital appreciation."

For other safe havens, consider shorter-duration bonds, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that invest in bonds with maturities of less than five years, as well as Treasury inflation-protected securities (TIPS) backed by the U.S. Treasury to guard against rising prices. Give a thought to value-oriented and defensive sectors, including consumer-staples, utilities and healthcare stocks, for retired investors who seek stability over higher returns. Your lifestyle, the balances in your retirement accounts, your goals, your financial profile - whether you have a mortgage, debt or long-term-care insurance - and your views on AI all play a role.

Pausing during a storm does not mean you suffer from paralysis, and you don't have to like the news in order to plan around it.

Your letter attests to that.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: CCTV4: Bringing Classical Chinese Poetry to the World Documentary Premiere One Poem, One World
data.description:
CCTV4: Bringing Classical Chinese Poetry to the World Documentary Premiere One Poem, One World

CCTV4: Bringing Classical Chinese Poetry to the World Documentary Premiere One Poem, One World

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Nov. 26, 2026

BEIJING, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Classical Chinese poetry has a history dating back thousands of years. It enjoyed a golden age during the Tang and Song dynasties, from the 8th to the 13th centuries, when poets such as Li Bai, Du Fu, Su Shi and Li Qingzhao flourished. Their works, while often depicting common human emotions and simple details of everyday life, are celebrated for their power also to embody the wisdom and spirit of the Chinese nation.

Yet, despite its ancient origins, classical Chinese poetry retains surprising resonance still today, as a brand new CMG television production reveals. Starting from the real-life experiences of several foreign nationals living in China, One Poem, One World employs accessible interpretations and authentic, moving stories to closely link classical poetry with contemporary life. By referring to Three Hundred Tang Poems, an anthology compiled in the mid-18th century, and Poems by a Thousand Masters, containing verses from both the Tang and the Song dynasties, One Poem, One World invites audiences in China and abroad to discover, through the medium of classical poetry, more about Chinese culture, and the lifestyle, values and spiritual pursuits of Chinese people.

Launched in conjunction with the 2026 World Chinese Language Conference, One Poem, One World aims, in six episodes, to promote Chinese language learning, the study of traditional Chinese culture and literary exchanges with other countries.

The first episode of One Poem, One World airs on CCTV-4, the Chinese International Channel of China Media Group, on November 29.

data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China, and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

data.title: TCL CSOT Showcases Value Chain Collaboration at DTC2026, From Materials to End-Device Applications
data.description:
TCL CSOT Showcases Value Chain Collaboration at DTC2026, From Materials to End-Device Applications

TCL CSOT Showcases Value Chain Collaboration at DTC2026, From Materials to End-Device Applications

PR Newswire

WUHAN, China, Nov. 26, 2026

WUHAN, China, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TCL CSOT's 2026 Global Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference (DTC2026), held under the theme "True Vision, AI in Motion," brought together partners from across the global display industry to showcase advances in materials, joint technology development, and end-device applications. The event highlighted how collaboration among upstream suppliers, panel manufacturers, and end-device partners can turn individual technological breakthroughs into integrated solutions and broader commercial applications, with IJP OLED at the center of TCL CSOT's practice.

Upstream Collaboration: Advancing Display Materials

At DTC2026, TCL CSOT and its upstream partners, including AGC, 3M, Merck, Summer Sprout, NOVATEK, Mitsubishi, SFC, SKMJ, and Idemitsu (IK), presented developments spanning advanced packaging, optical materials, display-driving technologies, and key materials for IJP OLED.

In advanced packaging, AGC showcased its TGV Glass Substrates for Advanced Packaging, featuring fine-pitch through-glass vias (TGVs) and high-precision through-glass via fabrication. The technology supports mass production of 510 × 515 mm large-format glass substrates for advanced packaging.

In optical materials, 3M presented several solutions for foldable displays, augmented reality (AR), and automotive applications. These included its Low Modulus Foldable OCA CEF94, Film-based Waveguide AR Glasses Demo, Optical Solution for Auto Under Display Camera, and Light Control Film for Auto OLED Display. CEF94 passed bending tests at temperatures as low as -30°C, helping reduce foldable-display creases under low-temperature conditions.

For emerging optical systems, Merck demonstrated its PB-Lens concept, which uses reactive mesogen (RM) materials and thin-film processing to explore the potential of planar lenses in virtual reality (VR) optical systems. Meanwhile, NOVATEK showcased its NOVA 14" WU + TED display and NOVA Privacy Display, highlighting advances in display-driving architecture and visual privacy that support lower-power designs and a wider range of end-device applications.

As IJP OLED advances toward broader commercialization, partners also presented key emissive materials and printing inks. Summer Sprout'sY4 red IJP-ink achieves 100% DCI-P3 color gamut coverage and improves device lifetime by more than 40% compared with the Y3 material system. Mitsubishi's IJP FLB INK uses solution-processable B Prime materials, increasing device brightness and efficiency (BI) by 10% while maintaining stable lifetime performance. SFC's IJP EML-B INK features BH-BD materials with approximately 50% improved solubility, supporting precision inkjet printing for high-PPI displays. SKMJ's IJP Blue Dopant delivers approximately 30% longer device lifetime than the Y3 system, while Idemitsu's IJP Blue Host improves Y4 device efficiency by 4% over Y3 through optimized molecular structures and host-guest matching.

Together, these developments across red, blue, and host materials strengthen the material foundation for IJP OLED. By bringing upstream materials expertise together with TCL CSOT's panel R&D and manufacturing capabilities, these collaborations help align materials development with actual product requirements and support the broader commercialization of IJP OLED technology.

Bringing Display Technologies into End-Device Applications

At DTC2026, TCL CSOT joined Lenovo, MSI, TAL Education Group, and VOYAH to showcase applications across laptops, desktop monitors, gaming handhelds, smart education, and automotive displays.

With Lenovo, TCL CSOT presented products across PC and professional display segments. The Lenovo Legion R9000P 16.0 WQ IJP OLED Display combines a 2560 × 1600 resolution with a 240Hz refresh rate. Its Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement reduces color fringing around text, supporting both clear text and smooth gaming visuals. The Lenovo Legion Y900 11 features an 11.1-inch 3.8K LTPS display with a 144Hz refresh rate, delivering high-resolution visuals and smooth performance to mobile entertainment and content creation. Meanwhile, the ThinkVision P27UL-40, a 27-inch 4K IJP OLED professional monitor, combines a 120Hz refresh rate with high color gamut coverage to support business productivity and professional creative work.

TCL CSOT and MSI jointly presented devices for gaming and business use. The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ features an 8-inch 120Hz IPS display with Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), helping deliver smoother gaming visuals. The MSI Prestige 14 AI+ uses a 14-inch IJP OLED display, combining wide color gamut coverage with a fast response time for mobile productivity and creative applications. For desktop users, the MSI PRO MAX OLED 271UPJW12 IJP OLED Display features TCL CSOT's proprietary Real Stripe RGB pixel arrangement to improve text clarity and reduce color fringing. It also incorporates MSI OLED Auto Care technology, which uses Dynamic Data Cumulative Compensation (DCC) to perform background OLED maintenance automatically, without interrupting normal use. The MSI MAG 346CQDF E20 Dual-Mode Curved Gaming Monitor offers two display modes: 200Hz at full resolution and up to 400Hz in HD mode, catering to different gaming requirements.

Spanning an 8-inch gaming handheld, an 11.1-inch tablet, 14-inch laptops, and 27-inch desktop monitors, these products illustrate how TCL CSOT and its end-device partners are adapting display technologies to different sizes, form factors, and user experiences.

Building a More Connected Display Ecosystem

At DTC2026, TCL CSOT highlighted efforts to extend partnerships beyond individual projects to technical standards, shared R&D platforms, and longer-term industry collaboration. Discussions included the new TÜV Rheinland Native Gaming Performance Display Standard, the Wuhan Joint Laboratory, and related ecosystem partnerships. TCL CSOT's IJP OLED roadmap across its t12 and t8 facilities also creates opportunities to coordinate materials, manufacturing processes, and end-device requirements across the supply chain, supporting the development and large-scale application of emerging display technologies.

From materials innovation by AGC, 3M, and Merck to end-device applications with Lenovo, MSI, and TAL Education Group, DTC2026 demonstrated how expertise across the value chain can turn technological advances into practical applications. Looking ahead, TCL CSOT will continue to work with global partners across materials research, panel manufacturing, and end-device applications, bringing together expertise from across the value chain to advance display technologies and expand and develop a more open, connected ecosystem.

About TCL CSOT

Established in 2009, TCL China Star Optoelectronics Technology Co., Ltd. (TCL CSOT) is a leading global innovator in display technologies. Its LCD, OLED, and MLED solutions power applications across TVs, smartphones, tablets, laptops, monitors, automotive systems, VR/XR, and commercial displays. With a clear strategic direction set by its advanced display technology brand APEX, TCL CSOT invests continuously and strategically in R&D, driven by a mission to amaze, protect and inspire all people through endlessly innovative display technology. As part of TCL's Worldwide Olympic Partnership, TCL CSOT is proud to deliver display solutions that elevate experiences on the global stage.
